newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel sees year-end German debt at 60.5 pct/GDP.
newsitem.headline: Waigel sees year-end German debt at 60.5 pct/GDP.

text.p: Germany's national debt will probably stand at 60.5 percent of gross domestic product by the end of this year, according to a paper by Finance Minister Theo Waigel which was published on Wednesday.

The debt will thus be slightly above the 60 percent reference value specified by the Maastricht treaty governing which countries are eligible to join European economic and monetary union at its planned start in 1999.

The paper notes, however, that Germany's debt still ranked as the third lowest in the Group of Seven countries and the fifth lowest in the European Union despite the extra burdens arising from the country's unification in 1990.

Of total debts at 2.22 trillion marks, some 570 billion are a result of unification. Without them, Germany's debt-to-GDP ratio would be 45.7 percent -- the lowest in the G7 and the second lowest in the EU, Waigel wrote.
